method: Foot normal >1e-7 at 1.25 ms substeps, foot-contact runs bridge at most two silent substeps. In complete runs, compare first and last positive normal impulses for rear-toe two segments and front-toe six segments. Equal substep means unresolved order, not simultaneous biological contact. Group sums can mix toe segments and do not establish plantar identity or biological timing; thresholds and gap merging are engineering choices. Used development seed and 4–6 s only.

corvid_reference.observation: Hallux contact precedes front toe contact; hallux leaves before the third digit in filmed steps on thin cork; distal toe flexes after leaving the ground and extends later in recovery. Surface and species limits apply. No American-crow angle or timing transfer is asserted.
